extracted.intended_audience: professional and serious amateur astronomers, planetary observers, and historians of planetary science
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and empirical criteria for observing, recording, and interpreting Martian surface markings (canals, oases, polar rifts) using telescopic drawings, cartouches, seasonal dating, and comparative historical charts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of mean-canal cartouches (composite analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mean-canal cartouches show synthetically the laws of the flux of the canals; composites are more conclusive because they summarize many observations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct composite (mean) cartouches from multiple drawings to establish broad laws of behavior; include mid-latitude and mid-longitude in the margin. Use composite charts to demonstrate that changes are intrinsic rather than optical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document individual constituents through sequential drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual drawings of a single canal at successive stages impart vividness and reveal the process of evolution in a way composites cannot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce dated sequential sketches across a season/opposition (as in the Brontes series) to capture stage-by-stage changes; use these alongside composites to show lifelike development of a feature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide long canals into sections for separate analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: A long canal may be divided into sections and each section treated as if it were a separate canal for cartouche determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose natural junctions/landmarks to split a canal (example: five sections between Propropontis and Sinus Titanum with lengths 12°, 16°, 15°, 12°, 13°). Find cartouches for each section to detect local timing/behavior differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule out extrinsic optical causes before concluding intrinsic change
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes in visibility must not be attributable to distance, definition, phase, or seeing — contrariety of behavior relative to these factors indicates intrinsic change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show that a canal waxes or wanes in exact opposition to distance/seeing (e.g., became less visible as planet neared) to eliminate extrinsic explanations. Explicitly address and negate alternative optical causes in analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require multiple observations across oppositions/seasons to detect hibernation (secular change)
rubrics_metrics.description: A canal may 'hibernate'—be absent for many Martian years—so long-term, repeated observation across oppositions is required to document secular absence or return.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare observations spanning many oppositions (years). Document presence/absence at each opposition to identify long-term dormancy vs seasonal fading (example: Thoth/Triton/Nepenthes seen in 1877–1888 but absent in 1894 until reappearing later).

rubrics_metrics.name: Date phenomena by seasonal longitudes (Martian calendar)
rubrics_metrics.description: Label observations by seasonal longitude to situate phenomena in the Martian year; ordering by seasonal longitude distinguishes seasonal from secular changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record and use seasonal longitude when tabulating appearances; arranging observations by seasonal longitude reveals patterns (first seasonal changes, then secular ones) and timing relationships among features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test separate identity vs observational error when portrayals differ
rubrics_metrics.description: When two differing portrayals of a marking occur, consider that they may be two separate canals rather than mistake or displacement of a single feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare dates, positions, and seasonal longitudes; if one feature appears while the other does not (and vice versa), treat them as distinct entities unless evidence shows otherwise (example: Amenthes vs Thoth alternation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use positional coincidence of polar rifts and later arctic canals to infer connection
rubrics_metrics.description: Rifts observed in the polar cap at one season often occupy the exact position later occupied by arctic canals once the cap melts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map rifts (dates, longitudes) and compare with later canal positions; compile identifications (as tabled: Hypanis, Hippalus, Rhombites, Python, Zygatis) to support the hypothesis that rifts and canals are seasonal states of the same feature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infer water/vegetation linkage from temporal sequence (cap melting → canal development)
rubrics_metrics.description: Canal visibility increases after polar cap disintegration; the sequence suggests water released from the caps enables vegetal growth that darkens canals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate that canals 'quicken into growth' only after the cap retreats and the polar fringe appears. Use timing delays and spatial progression (pole-to-equator wave) to support the water/vegetation causal model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze combination cartouches to compare constituents with mean behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: A combination cartouche (sum of constituents) can resemble the mean-canal cartouche even when the individual constituents behave anomalously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create cartouches for each constituent and for their combination; inspect how combination behavior may mask anomalous individual patterns (example: Thoth-Nepenthes-Triton broken bow vs Amenthes straight arrow).

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterize oases kinematics by tone change more than area change
rubrics_metrics.description: Oases tend to develop by deepening of tint (from a small nucleus outward) and later fade back to a nucleus rather than by large area expansion/contraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure both tone and apparent area over time; expect nuclei perhaps ~20 miles, growing to 75–100 miles in width by deepening of tone. Watch for core-first or rim-first fading patterns (example: Ascraeus Lucus showing a dark rim and lighter kernel).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat optical-artifact hypotheses cautiously and seek corroboration
rubrics_metrics.description: When an unusual appearance might be optical, do not assume it; instead check for corroborating occurrences in other spots, repeat observations, and cross-observer agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note the context (season, nearby features, seeing). If the effect is not seen elsewhere under similar conditions, lean toward objective cause but demand multiple independent confirmations before firm interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify observational sampling and publish date-by-date drawing counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Report numbers of drawings/observations by date ranges to give weight to cartouches and composite analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide counts per observation window (example given: Jan 21-25:12 drawings; Feb 23-Mar 2:15; Mar 28-Apr 5:14; Apr 26-May 8:27; Jun 3-16:6; Jul 11-21:16; total 90). Use sample size to justify composite reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note latitudinal timing differences (shearing) in development
rubrics_metrics.description: Cartouches show that similar-shaped curves are 'sheered' rightward with increasing latitude, meaning activity occurs later at more northerly latitudes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reading cartouches down the page, expect action 'later and later as the latitude was north.' Use this to infer propagation timing of events across latitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record and analyze alternation phenomena between neighboring systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Neighboring canals (or canal systems) may alternate in visibility (one present while the other absent) on a secular or seasonal basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track alternating presence/absence, relate alternation to seasonal longitude and cartouche curves, and consider alternation when reconciling differing historical depictions (example: Amenthes alternates with Thoth).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-validate current observations against historical charts (e.g., Schiaparelli)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare present drawings to earlier published charts and memoirs to validate identifications and detect genuine changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use previous observers' maps/labels to identify continuity or replacement of features, but remain open to re-identification when new patterns (e.g., doubling or gemination) appear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use phenology curves to contrast Earth vs Mars and justify causal interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Phenology curves show that on Mars the wave of vegetative quickening follows water (pole-to-equator) rather than the sun (equator-to-pole), supporting a water-limited model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plot 'dead point of vegetation' markers by latitude and time; compare Earth and Mars curves to show opposite bowed directions and use this to argue for a water-limited vegetative mechanism on Mars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for delays between cap melting and surface response when positing mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: A time lag between cap disintegration and canal/vegetation visibility is expected; any proposed mechanism must explain the observed delay (e.g., time for water percolation and plant sprouting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate plausible biological/geophysical timescales and show that observed delays are consistent; use delays as evidence against simple direct transference explanations and in favor of processes requiring development time.
